parts.t: Sumas Mountain is on the south side of the Fraser River in east Abbotsford. It is mostly natural land, with rural homes, some farms and a large regional park. It has its own set of rural land rules.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 12, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the official sources noted on this page. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Abbotsford.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Before you buy or sell, check the zoning, what the community plan says, and which schools serve the address.

Sumas Mountain has its own set of rural land rules.
The City’s Sumas Mountain profile says the area follows its own rules, the Sumas Mountain Rural Land Use Bylaw (Area H).
The Sumas Mountain Forest Service Road is looked after by the Province (Ministry of Forests), not the City.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Sumas Mountain

parts.t: and ask the City of Abbotsford how the property is zoned and what that allows.
If the home is on a well, test how much water it gives and how clean it is, and ask for past test results.
Find out how old the system is and when it was last serviced, and have it inspected.
Ask whether barns, shops, arenas and suites were built with permits.
Look for any rules or rights that others have over the land (covenants, rights of way and easements), including any access you rely on.
Rules about how close you can build to a stream can limit where you build. Ask the City of Abbotsford about any watercourse on or near the land.
